title: Color vs. Black-and-White Landscape Processing: Basic Tools and Non-Destructive Workflow
summary: The video contrasts color and black-and-white landscape processing and presents a concise, non-destructive workflow using Photoshop, Camera Raw (ACR/RAW) and a history-based system. The instructor crops to a 4x5 composition, then proceeds with zone-based edits (sky, trees, water) to guide the viewer’s eye, applying diffusion, dehaze, and selective brightness. A history-state approach replaces traditional layers, enabling rapid, brush-based adjustments that can be freely remixed. The middle ground receives atmosphere via fog-like effects (Gaussian blur), while foreground elements are toned and desaturated to balance color with tonal contrast. The sequence culminates in a full black-and-white conversion with dodge/burn work and creative refinements (sunbeams/clouds), followed by philosophy about practice and the roles of tools versus artistic intent.

sections.title: Color vs. Black & White Philosophy
sections.description: The speaker frames the comparison between processing color and black-and-white, asserting B&W is simpler (primarily dodge/burn) and color introduces more variables related to light and color interactions.

sections.title: Initial Color Processing & Crop Decision
sections.description: The image is prepared for color processing, with an explicit plan to crop the frame and set the project in a color workflow before further adjustments.

sections.title: Cropping & Zone Framing
sections.description: A deliberate crop to four-by-five is chosen to optimize composition, placing a tree on the edge and aligning mountain features to support the eye’s journey toward the waterfall.

sections.title: Zone-based Editing & Middle-ground Diffusion
sections.description: The shot is divided into three zones, with targeted diffusion and dehaze to push depth in the middle ground while protecting the sky and foreground from over-editing.

sections.title: History Brush & Non-destructive Workflow
sections.description: A non-destructive workflow is demonstrated using history states and a history brush, allowing rapid undo/redo and selective reapplication of adjustments without traditional layering.

sections.title: Fogging with Gaussian Blur & Atmospheric Adjustments
sections.description: Gaussian blur is used to create atmospheric fog, with controlled opacity and edge handling to simulate depth and distance in the landscape.

sections.title: Foreground Water & Rock Adjustments
sections.description: Adjustments focus on the stream and rocks: desaturate the gray foreground, elevate the water with a whites lift, and paint adjustments locally to balance tonal contrast.

sections.title: Sky, Vignette & Tone-based RAW Color Adjustments
sections.description: A dark vignette is applied to draw the eye inward, followed by a tonal-based color adjustment in RAW to reintroduce light with saturation controlled to preserve color harmony.

sections.title: Black & White Finalization & Creative Dodge/Burn
sections.description: The process moves to a full black-and-white conversion (preserving RGB), then an extensive dodge/burn pass to sculpt light, add fog, and introduce creative elements such as sunbeams and clouds for mood.
